extracted.subtask_description: Practical principles and criteria for creating and evaluating plot in fiction — how events, beats, choices, and structure generate tension and resolve meaningfully. Focuses on character-driven plotting, pacing, and avoiding common pitfalls like exposition dumps and plot holes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot is the sequence of narrative events experienced by the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of plot as the chain of events as they unfold for readers/viewers — not theme or mere premise. Evaluate whether the sequence is coherent as experienced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't equate plot with summary
rubrics_metrics.description: People asking 'What's the plot?' want a summary, not a tedious 'and then' list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing plot, focus on stakes, conflict, and driving questions rather than a beat-by-beat synopsis. Avoid mistaking a list of events for meaningful plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot as invisible skeleton
rubrics_metrics.description: A good plot is like a skeleton: critical, yet invisible — plots function structurally but should remain hidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot should support the story without drawing attention to itself; structural scaffolding must be present but not obtrusive or mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causality and coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Shit's gotta make sense, son — Events must fit together with logical progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that events follow plausibly from prior actions or motivations; avoid scenes that feel arbitrary or contradictory to established logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalating conflict to resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The quintessential plot — conflict escalates progressively until resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot should raise stakes over time, building pressure toward a satisfying payoff; flat or static conflict undermines momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction seeks conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: In life we avoid conflict, in fiction we seek it — tension drives narrative momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize obstacles and friction that force characters to act; conflict is the engine of plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Want versus fear
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot emerges from desires conflicting with fears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear wants (goals) and fears (what's at risk) for characters; the interplay should generate plot pressure and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grow the plot organically
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow the plot, don't build it — plots develop organically rather than being artificially constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let events arise naturally from character and situation rather than forcing contrived set-pieces; avoid over-schematic plotting that feels fabricated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The tension and recoil of choice and consequence — decisions create branching narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure choices have meaningful consequences that change direction or stakes; agency should matter and ripple through the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot as promise and payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot is promise — Events foreshadow eventual payoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish expectations and hints early so later developments feel earned; track setups and ensure corresponding payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters drive plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Let characters do the heavy lifting — Authentic plots emerge from character emotions and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize character motivation and reaction as causes for events; plots that happen 'to' characters rather than 'because of' them feel weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Chart the shortest point between beginning and end — Avoid unnecessarily convoluted routes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim detours and filler that don't serve character or theme; prefer clear, motivated progression over needless complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of plot holes
rubrics_metrics.description: On the subject of 'plot holes' — Stem from inattention, over-complexity, ignorance, or insufficient planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit for continuity, plausibility, and causal logic; simplify overly complex threads and fill gaps of knowledge or planning that create contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify tentpole events
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up your tentpoles — Identify critical events; ensure smooth connections between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map major beats (inciting incident, midpoint, climax, etc.) and make sure intervening scenes logically connect those pillars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pivot points
rubrics_metrics.description: The herky jerky plot shuffle pivot point boogie — Plots zigzag with multiple pivot points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include turning points and reversals that alter direction or stakes; these pivots keep momentum and surprise when motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot sets rhythm and pace
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot is the beat that sets the story's rhythm — Plot establishes pace aligned with emotional needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust scene length, intensity, and sequencing to match emotional arcs; pacing should serve dramatic needs, not arbitrary tempo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include tension release
rubrics_metrics.description: Every night needs a slow dance — Place tension release and false victories for respite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance tension with moments of relief and apparent wins to create emotional contrast and maintain reader stamina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track beats
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of my new band is 'Beat Sheet Manifesto' — Track beats to identify gaps and inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use beat sheets or similar tools to log scene beats and spot missing setups, lulls, or unearned events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of narrative units
rubrics_metrics.description: Beats become scenes become sequences become acts — Narrative units scale upward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coherence at each level (micro to macro); small beats should build scenes, scenes should build sequences, sequences should build acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subplots should complement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your sexy mistress, the subplot — Secondary storylines complement primary plots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design subplots to reinforce theme, character development, or stakes rather than distract; they should intersect meaningfully with the main plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use micro-plots for texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneath subplot, a nougaty layer of micro-plot — Small conflicts add texture without overwhelming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include low-stakes conflicts and moments that enrich character and world-building while avoiding cluttering the main arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exposition dumps
rubrics_metrics.description: Exposition is sand in the story's panties — Weave information into action; avoid dumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal backstory and world details through scenes, dialogue, and character choices; large blocks of tell-kernel weaken immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earn plot twists
rubrics_metrics.description: On the subject of the 'plot twist' — Genuine twists emerge organically from setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A twist must be foreshadowed and consistent with prior information; avoid surprises that violate established rules or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endings must resolve accumulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The ending is the answer to a very long equation — Endings feel inevitable when they resolve accumulated elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the finale the logical resolution of earlier choices, setups, and themes so the ending feels earned and inevitable rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot serves character and theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot is only means to an end — Plots serve characters and themes; readers care about meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize emotional truth, character growth, and thematic payoff over clever plotting for its own sake; meaning should drive structural choices.
